output.headline: Epic has made all four of its deals in the target's own sub-sector and pays 22.7x, above the comparable median of 21.4x.
output.differentiator: All four deals are in the target's own sub-sector, more than any other priority-list buyer, and its 22.7x median paid exceeds every financial sponsor on the list.
output.why_them: Same-sub-sector add-on; pays above the comparable median

acquirer_overview.title: A strategic buyer focused on Health IT, with four control deals
points: Four deals from 2018 to 2022, all control deals, all in Health IT and all in the target's own sub-sector [T:record, K:control_share].
Three of four closed (75%); median deal $240M, ranging from $15M to $767M [K:closed_share, T:record].
Third on the priority list of 10, from 107 buyers scored; no company profile was researched [R:rank, B:buyer].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Same sub-sector, similar margin profile, and a technology-led buying pattern
points: Share of deals in the target's sub-sector is the strongest factor in its likelihood; margin fit is a strong factor [S:sector_share, S:margin_fit].
Technology Capability drove 4 of 4 deals, against 10% of all deals in the file, a distinct motive [M:technology_capability].
Margin Improvement also appears in 4 of 4 deals; it has one deal in the target's National region [M:margin_improvement, T:record].

precedent_activity.title: Its latest and largest deals are close to the target's size
points: Crest Digital Health: $440M Strategic Acquisition, 2022, National, 22.7x EBITDA, closed [D:MA-2022-0213].
Meridian Health Analytics: $767M Platform Investment, 2018, 22.0x, closed. Charter Clinical Systems: $40M Carve-out, 2019, 24.4x, closed [D:MA-2018-0429, D:MA-2019-0351].
Oak Clinical Analytics, a $15M Merger of Equals in 2021 at 18.1x, was terminated [D:MA-2021-0372].

valuation_context.title: The median is defensible, and Epic's own pricing sits above it
points: Comparable range is 19.4x to 23.3x EBITDA (25th to 75th percentile), median 21.4x, across 13 same-sub-sector deals [V:comps].
Target margin of 25.0% is above the comparables' 22.2% median but not in their top quarter, so the 50th percentile is the anchor [V:comps].
Epic's median paid is 22.7x, between the comparable median and 75th percentile. Synergy headroom is $14M-$23M; buyer revenue was not researched [V:comps, V:synergy].

risk_flags.title: Execution record
risk_flags.concern: One of four deals terminated, so closure is 75%.
risk_flags.mitigant: The terminated deal was the smallest, a $15M Merger of Equals in 2021.
risk_flags.reality: Three of four closed, including the $440M and $767M deals [K:closed_share, D:MA-2021-0372].

risk_flags.title: PE-backed seller
risk_flags.concern: Having bought from this kind of seller is a modest factor against Epic.
risk_flags.mitigant: Sub-sector share is the strongest factor and margin fit is strong.
risk_flags.reality: The seller-type signal is weaker than the factors in its favour [S:own_fit_s, S:sector_share].

risk_flags.title: Capacity and recency
risk_flags.concern: Buyer revenue is unresearched, and only one deal has come since 2022.
risk_flags.mitigant: It has funded a $767M deal and a $440M deal.
risk_flags.reality: Ability to pay is unverified beyond the $14M-$23M synergy headroom [V:synergy, K:recent, T:record].

conviction.rationale: Four deals in the target's own sub-sector, one in its region, and third on the priority list after review, so the evidence for this buyer is consistent [T:record, R:rank, C:conviction].
